def sample(
    self,
    shots: int,
    *,
    batch_size: int | None = None,
    prepend_observables: bool = False,
    append_observables: bool = False,
    separate_observables: bool = False,
    bit_packed: bool = False,
    use_detector_reference_sample: bool = False,
    use_observable_reference_sample: bool = False,
    postselection_mask: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray | tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Return detector samples from the circuit.

    The circuit must define the detectors using DETECTOR instructions. Observables
    defined by OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE instructions can also be included in the results
    as honorary detectors.

    Args:
        shots: The number of times to sample every detector in the circuit.
        batch_size: The number of samples to process in each batch. Defaults to
            None, which automatically chooses a batch size based on available
            memory. With ``strategy="active_statevector"`` a call is split
            into a batch per numba thread when each gets at least 4096 shots,
            or at least 256 that trajectory sharing may not keep on fewer
            lanes. With a stabilizer-rank strategy on a GPU, setting this
            explicitly can help fully utilize VRAM.
            NOTE: Changing the batch size will affect reproducibility even with
            a fixed seed.
        separate_observables: Defaults to False. When set to True, the return value
            is a (detection_events, observable_flips) tuple instead of a flat
            detection_events array.
        prepend_observables: Defaults to false. When set, observables are included
            with the detectors and are placed at the start of the results.
        append_observables: Defaults to false. When set, observables are included
            with the detectors and are placed at the end of the results.
        bit_packed: Defaults to false. When set, results are bit-packed. The
            packed rows may be a strided view of a wider array.
        use_detector_reference_sample: Defaults to False. When True, a noiseless
            reference sample is computed and XORed with detector outcomes so that
            results represent deviations from the noiseless baseline. This should
            only be used when detectors are deterministic. Otherwise, it can
            unpredictably change the results.
        use_observable_reference_sample: Defaults to False. When True, a noiseless
            reference sample is computed and XORed with observable outcomes so that
            results represent deviations from the noiseless baseline. This should
            only be used when observables are deterministic. Otherwise, it can
            unpredictably change the results.
        postselection_mask: Optional boolean array of length ``num_detectors``.
            When set, shots where any masked direct detector (an error bit
            or a constant) fires are not sampled further. All ``shots`` rows
            are still returned: survivors
            contain the full sample, while discarded rows retain direct detector
            columns and fill component columns with ``False``; with
            ``strategy="active_statevector"``, a shot discarded by a masked
            component detector also reads ``False`` in the outputs set after
            it. Re-apply the mask to the returned detector columns to recover
            surviving shots.

    Returns:
        A numpy array or tuple of numpy arrays containing the samples.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``separate_observables`` is combined with
            ``prepend_observables`` or ``append_observables``.

    """
    if separate_observables and (prepend_observables or append_observables):
        raise ValueError(
            "Can't specify separate_observables=True with "
            "append_observables=True or prepend_observables=True"
        )

    compute_reference = (
        use_detector_reference_sample or use_observable_reference_sample
    )
    num_detectors = self._num_detectors

    if postselection_mask is not None:
        mask = np.asarray(postselection_mask, dtype=np.bool_)
        if mask.shape != (num_detectors,):
            raise ValueError(
                f"postselection_mask must have shape ({num_detectors},), "
                f"got {mask.shape}"
            )
        # NOTE: without pruning, only direct detectors can skip any work.
        if not self._backend.prunes:
            skips = mask & self._direct_detector_mask
        else:
            skips = mask.copy()
        indices, flips, columns = self._direct_detectors
        constant = indices < 0
        skips[columns[constant]] &= flips[constant] & (
            not use_detector_reference_sample
        )
        postselection_mask = (
            mask if skips.any() and self._program.components else None
        )

    if (
        bit_packed
        and postselection_mask is None
        and not (prepend_observables or separate_observables)
    ):
        _check_sizes(shots, batch_size)
        num_outputs = (
            self._program.num_outputs if append_observables else num_detectors
        )
        packed = self._sample_direct_packed(shots, num_outputs)
        if packed is not None:
            return packed

    if postselection_mask is not None:
        referenced = None
        if compute_reference:
            is_detector = np.arange(self._program.num_outputs) < num_detectors
            referenced = np.where(
                is_detector,
                use_detector_reference_sample,
                use_observable_reference_sample,
            )
        samples = self._sample_batches_with_postselection(
            shots,
            batch_size,
            postselection_mask=postselection_mask,
            referenced=referenced,
        )
    elif compute_reference:
        samples, reference = self._sample_batches(
            shots, batch_size, compute_reference=True
        )
        if use_detector_reference_sample:
            samples[:, :num_detectors] ^= reference[:num_detectors]
        if use_observable_reference_sample:
            samples[:, num_detectors:] ^= reference[num_detectors:]
    else:
        samples = self._sample_batches(shots, batch_size)

    det_samples = samples[:, :num_detectors]
    obs_samples = samples[:, num_detectors:]

    if prepend_observables and append_observables:
        combined = np.concatenate([obs_samples, det_samples, obs_samples], axis=1)
        return _maybe_bit_pack(combined, bit_packed=bit_packed)
    if append_observables:
        return _maybe_bit_pack(samples, bit_packed=bit_packed)
    if prepend_observables:
        combined = np.concatenate([obs_samples, det_samples], axis=1)
        return _maybe_bit_pack(combined, bit_packed=bit_packed)
    if separate_observables:
        return (
            _maybe_bit_pack(det_samples, bit_packed=bit_packed),
            _maybe_bit_pack(obs_samples, bit_packed=bit_packed),
        )

    return _maybe_bit_pack(det_samples, bit_packed=bit_packed)

    strategy: SamplingStrategy = "active_statevector",
    seed: int | None = None,
    trajectory_sharing: bool | None = None,
):
    """Create a measurement sampler.

    Args:
        circuit: The quantum circuit to compile.
        strategy: "active_statevector" (the default), or a stabilizer rank
            decomposition strategy ("cat5", "bss", "cutting").
        trajectory_sharing: With ``strategy="active_statevector"``, simulate shots
            with equal histories on one lane. Defaults to True for
            ``"active_statevector"`` and False otherwise.
        seed: Random seed for the sampler. IMPORTANT: Currently, the sampler
            will only produce deterministic samples for fixed batch size. If
            deterministic samples are needed, the batch size should be set
            manually.

    """
    super().__init__(
        circuit,
        sample_detectors=False,
        mode="sequential",
        seed=seed,
        strategy=strategy,
        trajectory_sharing=trajectory_sharing,
    )

def probability_of(self, state: np.ndarray, *, batch_size: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Compute probabilities for a batch of error samples given a measurement state.

    Args:
        state: The measurement outcome state to compute probability for.
        batch_size: Number of error samples to use for estimation.

    Returns:
        Array of probabilities P(state | error_sample) for each error sample.

    """
    if batch_size < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"batch_size must be at least 1, got {batch_size}")
    expected_outputs = self._program.num_outputs
    if state.shape != (expected_outputs,):
        raise ValueError(
            f"state must have shape ({expected_outputs},), got {state.shape}"
        )
    f_samples = jnp.asarray(self._channel_sampler.sample(batch_size))
    p_norm = jnp.ones(batch_size)
    p_joint = jnp.ones(batch_size)

    if len(self._program.direct_f_indices) > 0:
        direct_bits = _direct_bits(self._program, f_samples)
        n_direct = len(self._program.direct_f_indices)
        targets = state[self._program.output_order[:n_direct]]
        p_joint = p_joint * (direct_bits == targets).all(axis=1)

    for component in self._program.components:
        assert isinstance(component, CompiledComponent)
        assert len(component.compiled_scalar_graphs) == 2

        f_selected = f_samples[:, component.f_selection]

        norm_circuit, joint_circuit = component.compiled_scalar_graphs

        # Normalization: only f-params
        p_norm = p_norm * jnp.abs(evaluate(norm_circuit, f_selected))

        # Joint probability: f-params + state
        component_state = state[list(component.output_indices)]
        tiled_state = jnp.tile(component_state, (batch_size, 1))
        joint_params = jnp.hstack([f_selected, tiled_state])
        p_joint = p_joint * jnp.abs(evaluate(joint_circuit, joint_params))

    return np.asarray(p_joint / p_norm)

def sample_program(
    program: CompiledProgram, f_params: jax.Array, key: PRNGKey
) -> jax.Array:
    """Sample all outputs of a program of stabilizer-rank components with JAX.

    Args:
        program: The compiled program to sample from.
        f_params: Error parameters, shape (batch_size, num_f_params).
        key: JAX random key.

    Returns:
        Samples array of shape (batch_size, num_outputs), reordered to
        match the original output indices.

    """
    if program.num_outputs == 0:
        return jnp.zeros((f_params.shape[0], 0), dtype=jnp.bool_)
    results = []
    if len(program.direct_f_indices) > 0:
        results.append(_direct_bits(program, f_params))
    for component in program.components:
        assert isinstance(component, CompiledComponent)
        samples, key, max_norm_deviation = sample_component(component, f_params, key)
        _check_norm(max_norm_deviation, component.norm_warning_threshold)
        results.append(samples)
    combined = jnp.concatenate(results, axis=1)
    if program.output_reindex is not None:
        combined = combined[:, program.output_reindex]
    return combined

def sample_statevector_program(
    program: CompiledProgram,
    f_params: np.ndarray,
    seed: int,
    layouts: tuple[SharingLayout, ...],
    direct_flips: np.ndarray,
    *,
    share: bool,
    sharing_stats: deque[dict] | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample all outputs of a program of statevector components, without JAX.

    Args:
        program: The compiled program to sample from.
        f_params: Error parameters, shape (batch_size, num_f_params).
        seed: Seed of the batch's random numbers, below 2^64.
        layouts: The sharing layout of each component.
        direct_flips: The flip of each direct output, with its reference bit.
        share: Whether shots with equal histories share a lane.
        sharing_stats: If given, the executor appends its lane counts.

    Returns:
        Samples array of shape (batch_size, num_outputs) in the original order.

    """
    rows = f_params.shape[0]
    results = []
    for index, (component, layout) in enumerate(
        zip(program.components, layouts, strict=True)
    ):
        assert isinstance(component, StatevectorComponent)
        component_seed = (seed + index * int(GOLDEN)) % 2**64
        samples, max_norm_deviation, stats = sample_shared_component(
            component, layout, f_params, component_seed, share
        )
        if sharing_stats is not None:
            sharing_stats.append(stats)
        _check_norm(max_norm_deviation, component.norm_warning_threshold)
        results.append(samples)
    component_bits = (
        np.concatenate(results, axis=1) if results else np.zeros((rows, 0), np.bool_)
    )
    out = np.empty((rows, program.num_outputs), dtype=np.bool_)
    _gather_outputs(
        out.size,
        f_params,
        program.direct_f_indices,
        direct_flips,
        component_bits,
        program.output_order,
        out,
    )
    return out

The scalar for each graph is a product of four exact term families and the floating-point FloatTerms family, multiplied by a per-graph ScalarPrefactor (an exact Dyadic factor with its 2^power2, and an approximate complex factor for angles that are not multiples of π/4). def compile_scalars(
    scalars: list[Scalar], param_ids: list[int]
) -> CompiledScalarGraphs:
    """Compile exact scalars, one per stabilizer term, into JAX arrays.

    Column ``k`` of the parameter values the result is evaluated on holds the bit
    of parameter ``param_ids[k]``. Each scalar is ``Scalar.simplified`` first,
    and zero scalars are dropped. Angles that are multiples of π/4 stay exact;
    other angles go into each term's float factor (terms without parameters) or
    into the float term family.

    Raises:
        KeyError: A term uses a parameter that is not in ``param_ids``.
        OverflowError: A Dyadic coefficient does not fit in int32.

    """
    column = {p: k for k, p in enumerate(param_ids)}
    n_params = len(param_ids)
    simplified = [s.simplified() for s in scalars]
    split = [_split_scalar(s, column, n_params) for s in simplified if not s.is_zero]

    def padded_field(
        family: str,
        index: int,
        shape: tuple[int, ...] = (),
        dtype: Any = np.uint8,
        fill: Any = 0,
    ) -> jax.Array:
        rows = [[term[index] for term in getattr(s, family)] for s in split]
        return _padded(rows, shape, dtype, fill)

    def counts(family: str) -> jax.Array:
        return jnp.array([len(getattr(s, family)) for s in split], dtype=jnp.int32)

    mask = (n_params,)
    return CompiledScalarGraphs(
        num_graphs=len(split),
        n_params=n_params,
        node_phases=NodePhases(
            phases=padded_field("nodes", 0),
            params=padded_field("nodes", 1, mask),
            counts=counts("nodes"),
        ),
        phase_terms=PhaseTerms(
            coeffs=padded_field("phases", 0), params=padded_field("phases", 1, mask)
        ),
        pi_products=PiProducts(
            psi_params=padded_field("pi_pairs", 0, mask),
            phi_params=padded_field("pi_pairs", 1, mask),
        ),
        phase_pairs=PhasePairs(
            alpha=padded_field("phase_pairs", 0),
            alpha_params=padded_field("phase_pairs", 2, mask),
            beta=padded_field("phase_pairs", 1),
            beta_params=padded_field("phase_pairs", 3, mask),
            counts=counts("phase_pairs"),
        ),
        float_terms=FloatTerms(
            table=padded_field("floats", 0, (4,), np.complex64, fill=1),
            a_params=padded_field("floats", 1, mask),
            b_params=padded_field("floats", 2, mask),
        ),
        prefactor=_scalar_prefactor(split),
    )

Each exact term family (NodePhases, PhaseTerms, PiProducts, PhasePairs) computes its own contribution via .evaluate(param_vals). This function multiplies those together with the per-graph ScalarPrefactor and merges power2 into the exponent of the exact product before converting to floating point, so the powers of two cannot overflow or underflow separately. Any approximate floatfactor is multiplied in afterwards. The floating-point FloatTerms family (angles that are not multiples of π/4) is multiplied in only when the circuit has float terms.

@jax.jit
def evaluate(circuit: CompiledScalarGraphs, param_vals: Array) -> Array:
    """Evaluate compiled circuit with batched parameter values.

    Each exact term family (``NodePhases``, ``PhaseTerms``, ``PiProducts``,
    ``PhasePairs``) computes its own contribution via ``.evaluate(param_vals)``.
    This function multiplies those together with the per-graph
    ``ScalarPrefactor`` and merges ``power2`` into the exponent of the exact
    product before converting to floating point, so the powers of two cannot
    overflow or underflow separately. Any approximate floatfactor is multiplied
    in afterwards. The floating-point ``FloatTerms`` family (angles that are not
    multiples of π/4) is multiplied in only when the circuit has float terms.

    Args:
        circuit: Compiled circuit representation.
        param_vals: Bits of the compiled parameters (error-basis bits, then
            output bits), shape ``(batch_size, n_params)``.

    Returns:
        Complex array of shape ``(batch_size,)``: the summed scalars per sample.

    """
    prefactor = circuit.prefactor
    if prefactor.power2.shape[0] == 0:
        return jnp.zeros(param_vals.shape[0], dtype=jnp.complex64)

    exact_prefactor = ExactScalarArray(prefactor.floatfactor, prefactor.power2)

    total = functools.reduce(
        operator.mul,
        [
            circuit.node_phases.evaluate(param_vals),
            circuit.phase_terms.evaluate(param_vals),
            circuit.pi_products.evaluate(param_vals),
            circuit.phase_pairs.evaluate(param_vals),
            exact_prefactor,
        ],
    )
    if not prefactor.has_approximate_floatfactors and not circuit.has_float_terms:
        return total.sum().to_complex()

    return jnp.sum(
        total.to_complex()
        * circuit.float_terms.evaluate(param_vals)
        * prefactor.approximate_floatfactors,
        axis=-1,
    )

def classify_direct(component: Graph, layout: ParamLayout) -> tuple[int, bool] | None:
    """Return ``(basis index, flip)`` for a direct output; index -1 means constant.

    That is the case when the component is a classical output boundary joined by
    a Hadamard edge to a classical Z spider whose phase is 0 or π plus at most
    one error-basis parameter.
    """
    outputs = component.outputs()
    if len(outputs) != 1 or component.num_vertices() != 2:
        return None
    (out,) = outputs
    (spider,) = component.neighbors(out)
    # NOTE: zxparam never lets a classical boundary touch a quantum vertex, so a
    # classical output implies a classical spider.
    if component.vertex_domain(out) == Domain.QUANTUM:
        return None
    if component.vertex_type(spider) != VertexType.Z:
        return None
    if component.edge_type(out, spider) != EdgeType.HADAMARD:
        return None
    phase = component.phase(spider)
    if len(phase.parameters) > 1 or phase.value not in (0, 1):
        return None
    if not phase.parameters:
        return -1, phase.value == 1
    (param,) = phase.parameters
    kind, basis_index = layout.kind(param)
    if kind != "f":
        return None
    return basis_index, phase.value == 1

Otherwise its outputs are plugged (all prefixes in sequential mode, none and all in joint mode), each plugged graph is decomposed into stabilizer terms, and the terms are compiled into JAX arrays.

def compile_program(
    prepared: SamplingGraph,
    *,
    mode: DecompositionMode,
    strategy: SamplingStrategy,
) -> CompiledProgram:
    """Compile a prepared graph into an executable sampling program.

    The graph is split into connected components. A component whose single
    output equals one error-basis bit or a constant takes the direct path. With
    ``strategy="active_statevector"`` every other component becomes an action tape for
    the statevector executor. Otherwise its outputs are plugged (all prefixes
    in ``sequential`` mode, none and all in ``joint`` mode), each plugged graph
    is decomposed into stabilizer terms, and the terms are compiled into JAX
    arrays.

    Args:
        prepared: The prepared graph from ``prepare_graph``.
        mode: ``"sequential"`` for sampling, ``"joint"`` for probabilities.
        strategy: ``"active_statevector"``, or a stabilizer-rank decomposition
            strategy.

    Returns:
        A CompiledProgram ready for sampling.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``strategy="active_statevector"`` is combined with ``mode="joint"``.

    """
    if strategy == "active_statevector":
        if mode == "joint":
            raise ValueError(
                "strategy='active_statevector' samples outcomes and cannot compute "
                f"probabilities. {STABILIZER_RANK_HINT}"
            )
        compile_component = compile_statevector_component
    else:
        compile_component = partial(_compile_component, mode=mode, strategy=strategy)
    graph = prepared.graph
    layout = prepared.layout

    direct_entries: list[tuple[int, int, bool]] = []
    compiled_components: list[CompiledComponent | StatevectorComponent] = []
    compiled_output_order: list[int] = []

    components = sorted(graph.connected_components(), key=lambda c: len(c.outputs()))
    for component in components:
        output_indices = [_port(component, v) for v in component.outputs()]
        direct = classify_direct(component, layout)
        if direct is not None:
            basis_index, flip = direct
            direct_entries.append((output_indices[0], basis_index, flip))
            continue
        compiled_components.append(compile_component(component, output_indices, layout))
        compiled_output_order.extend(output_indices)

    # Sort direct entries by output index so that — together with the output
    # prioritisation in transform_error_basis — the concatenated layout often
    # matches the original output order, sparing a reindex at sample time.
    direct_entries.sort()
    output_order = np.array(
        [e[0] for e in direct_entries] + compiled_output_order, dtype=np.int32
    )
    reindex = np.argsort(output_order)
    is_identity = np.array_equal(reindex, np.arange(len(output_order)))

    return CompiledProgram(
        components=tuple(compiled_components),
        direct_f_indices=np.array([e[1] for e in direct_entries], dtype=np.int32),
        direct_flips=np.array([e[2] for e in direct_entries], dtype=np.bool_),
        output_order=output_order,
        output_reindex=None if is_identity else reindex,
        num_outputs=prepared.num_outputs,
        num_detectors=prepared.num_detectors,
    )

docs.title: terms
docs.text:
Term-family modules for compiled scalar graphs.

Each compiled scalar is the product of four exact term families (NodePhases, PhaseTerms, PiProducts, PhasePairs) and a floating-point family (FloatTerms, for angles that are not multiples of π/4), times a per-graph prefactor (ScalarPrefactor). This module defines the families as equinox.Module records, bundles the shared phase tables, and gives each family an evaluate method that turns a batch of binary parameter values into an ExactScalarArray (or, for FloatTerms, a complex array).

Downstream, compile.py builds instances of these classes from zxparam scalars (compile_scalars), and evaluate.py orchestrates the products.

def evaluate(self, param_vals: Array) -> Array:
    """Evaluate the product per graph, batched over ``param_vals``.

    Args:
        param_vals: Binary parameter values, shape ``(batch, n_params)``.

    Returns:
        Complex array of shape ``(batch, num_graphs)``.

    """
    pa = matmul_gf2(self.a_params, param_vals).astype(jnp.int32)
    pb = matmul_gf2(self.b_params, param_vals).astype(jnp.int32)
    index = pa + 2 * pb
    table = jnp.broadcast_to(self.table[None], (*index.shape, 4))
    values = jnp.take_along_axis(table, index[..., None], axis=-1)[..., 0]
    return jnp.prod(values, axis=-1)

def evaluate(self, param_vals: Array) -> ExactScalarArray:
    """Evaluate Π (1 + ω^(4·parity + phase)) per graph, batched over param_vals.

    Args:
        param_vals: Binary parameter values, shape ``(batch, n_params)``.

    Returns:
        ``ExactScalarArray`` of shape ``(batch, num_graphs)``.

    """
    rowsum = matmul_gf2(self.params, param_vals)
    phase_idx = (4 * rowsum + self.phases) % 8

    term_vals = _ONE_PLUS_PHASES[phase_idx]
    mask = jnp.arange(self.phases.shape[1])[None, :] < self.counts[:, None]
    term_vals = jnp.where(mask[..., None], term_vals, _IDENTITY)

    return ExactScalarArray(term_vals).prod(axis=-1)

def evaluate(self, param_vals: Array) -> ExactScalarArray:
    """Evaluate Π (1 + ω^α + ω^β - ω^(α+β)) per graph, batched.

    Args:
        param_vals: Binary parameter values, shape ``(batch, n_params)``.

    Returns:
        ``ExactScalarArray`` of shape ``(batch, num_graphs)``.

    """
    rowsum_a = matmul_gf2(self.alpha_params, param_vals)
    rowsum_b = matmul_gf2(self.beta_params, param_vals)

    alpha = (self.alpha + rowsum_a * 4) % 8
    beta = (self.beta + rowsum_b * 4) % 8
    gamma = (alpha + beta) % 8

    term_vals = (
        _IDENTITY + UNIT_PHASES[alpha] + UNIT_PHASES[beta] - UNIT_PHASES[gamma]
    )
    mask = jnp.arange(self.alpha.shape[1])[None, :] < self.counts[:, None]
    term_vals = jnp.where(mask[..., None], term_vals, _IDENTITY)

    return ExactScalarArray(term_vals).prod(axis=-1)

Each term is stored as k = 4·α mod 8 ∈ 0..7 and evaluates to ω^(k·⊕params) with ω = e^(iπ/4). Terms sharing a parameter bitstring have been combined to a single stored coefficient (see compile_scalars).

def evaluate(self, param_vals: Array) -> ExactScalarArray:
    """Evaluate ω^(Σ coeffs · parity) per graph, batched over param_vals.

    Args:
        param_vals: Binary parameter values, shape ``(batch, n_params)``.

    Returns:
        ``ExactScalarArray`` of shape ``(batch, num_graphs)``.

    """
    rowsum = matmul_gf2(self.params, param_vals)
    phase_idx = (rowsum * self.coeffs) % 8
    total_phase = jnp.sum(phase_idx, axis=-1) % 8
    return ExactScalarArray(UNIT_PHASES[total_phase])

def evaluate(self, param_vals: Array) -> ExactScalarArray:
    """Evaluate Π (-1)^(ψ·φ) per graph as a real ±1 exact scalar.

    Args:
        param_vals: Binary parameter values, shape ``(batch, n_params)``.

    Returns:
        ``ExactScalarArray`` of shape ``(batch, num_graphs)``, with values
        in {+1, -1} represented exactly.

    """
    psi = matmul_gf2(self.psi_params, param_vals)
    phi = matmul_gf2(self.phi_params, param_vals)

    exponent = (psi * phi) % 2
    sum_exponents = jnp.sum(exponent, axis=-1) % 2

    # (1 - 2·bit) ∈ {+1, -1}; promote to the 4-coefficient ExactScalar basis.
    summands_exact = (1 - 2 * sum_exponents)[..., None] * _IDENTITY
    return ExactScalarArray(summands_exact)

Per-graph static scalar prefactor — independent of parameter values.

Each graph's value is the product of the four exact term families and FloatTerms times the prefactor floatfactor · 2^power2 (which includes any global phase that is a multiple of π/4), times the graph's complex entry of approximate_floatfactors. That entry collects the parameter-free factors whose angles are not multiples of π/4 (see _split_scalar in compile.py): a global phase whose denominator is outside {1, 2, 4}, and parameter-free NodeTerms and PhasePairs with such angles. It is 1 when a graph has none of them.

This class is pure data; the final fold-in with the term-family product (which branches on has_approximate_floatfactors and on CompiledScalarGraphs.has_float_terms) lives in evaluate.py.

docs.title: builder
docs.text:
GraphBuilder: the ZX graph of a stim circuit and its bookkeeping.

GraphBuilder owns the graph while a circuit is parsed: wire ends, measurement records, error bits, pending correlated errors, and detectors and observables. The gate library (tsim.core.instructions) builds on its methods and never adds vertices itself; build returns the finished open or closed graph.

Qubit wires are quantum. Every wire vertex starts as a quantum boundary, and gates turn a wire's trailing boundary into a spider in place (see GraphBuilder.spider), so the spider stays quantum. Only measurements (merge_mirror_copies) and detector and observable annotations create classical vertices. NOTE: zxparam's Graph.add_vertex defaults to the classical domain, so wire vertices are only ever added here.

Record a noise channel and allocate its error bits.

def add_channel(self, probs: np.ndarray) -> int:
    """Record a noise channel and allocate its error bits.

    ``probs`` is the channel's distribution over its ``k`` error bits, so it
    has ``2^k`` entries. Returns the first bit; the channel owns bits
    ``first … first + k − 1``. Raises ``ValueError`` if the number of
    entries is not a power of two.
    """
    num_bits = channel_num_bits(probs)
    first = self._num_error_bits
    self._channel_probs.append(probs)
    self._num_error_bits += num_bits
    return first

def add_detector(self, record_indices: list[int]) -> None:
    """Add a detector that XORs the given measurement records."""
    v0 = self._graph.add_vertex(
        VertexType.X,
        col=self._annotation_col(record_indices),
        row=ANNOTATION_ROW,
        domain=Domain.CLASSICAL,
        label=f"det[{len(self._detectors)}]",
    )
    for record_index in record_indices:
        self._xor_record(v0, record_index)
    self._detectors.append(v0)

docs.title: build
docs.text:
build(*, closed: bool, outputs: Outputs) -> Graph

Return the circuit's graph with its wires closed or given ports.

With closed=False, qubit q's wire start, if it is still a boundary, gets input port -(q + 1) and its end gets output port q. With closed=True, wire starts that are still boundaries become |0⟩ (a quantum X(0) spider) and wire ends are discarded. Helper lanes (negative indices, used by MPP, MPAD and heralded channels) are always discarded at the end.

outputs picks the classical output boundaries, whose ports follow the qubit outputs (from 0 when closed):

  • "detectors": one per detector, then one per observable; the det[i] / obs[k] labels move to them.
  • "records": one per measurement record; the rec[i] labels move to them.
  • "none": no classical outputs.

Detector and observable spiders are removed unless they are the outputs. In open graphs, measurement spiders that are not outputs keep their rec[i] / m[i] labels; closed graphs are meant to be reduced, so only their output boundaries carry labels, which survive reduction.

An open graph's tensor is the circuit's channel together with the output bits; for bound error parameters, a closed graph's tensor is the joint distribution of its outputs. The builder is unchanged, so it can build again.

Source code in src/tsim/core/builder.py 
def build(self, *, closed: bool, outputs: Outputs) -> Graph:
    """Return the circuit's graph with its wires closed or given ports.

    With ``closed=False``, qubit ``q``'s wire start, if it is still a
    boundary, gets input port ``-(q + 1)`` and its end gets output port
    ``q``. With ``closed=True``, wire starts that are still boundaries become
    ``|0⟩`` (a quantum X(0) spider) and wire ends are discarded. Helper lanes
    (negative indices, used by MPP, MPAD and heralded channels) are always
    discarded at the end.

    ``outputs`` picks the classical output boundaries, whose ports follow the
    qubit outputs (from 0 when closed):

    - ``"detectors"``: one per detector, then one per observable; the
      ``det[i]`` / ``obs[k]`` labels move to them.
    - ``"records"``: one per measurement record; the ``rec[i]`` labels move
      to them.
    - ``"none"``: no classical outputs.

    Detector and observable spiders are removed unless they are the outputs.
    In open graphs, measurement spiders that are not outputs keep their
    ``rec[i]`` / ``m[i]`` labels; closed graphs are meant to be reduced, so
    only their output boundaries carry labels, which survive reduction.

    An open graph's tensor is the circuit's channel together with the output
    bits; for bound error parameters, a closed graph's tensor is the joint
    distribution of its outputs. The builder is unchanged, so it can build
    again.
    """
    if outputs not in get_args(Outputs):
        raise ValueError(
            f"outputs must be one of {get_args(Outputs)}, got {outputs!r}"
        )
    self._check_finalized()
    g = self._graph.copy()
    self._align_wire_ends(g)
    if closed:
        for v in self._first_vertex.values():
            if g.vertex_type(v) == VertexType.BOUNDARY:
                g.plug_basis(v)
        for v in self._last_vertex.values():
            g.discard(v)
        first_port = 0
    else:
        for q, v in self._first_vertex.items():
            if q >= 0 and g.vertex_type(v) == VertexType.BOUNDARY:
                g.set_port(v, -(q + 1))
        for q, v in self._last_vertex.items():
            if q >= 0:
                g.set_port(v, q)
            else:
                g.discard(v)
        first_port = max((q for q in self._last_vertex if q >= 0), default=-1) + 1
    if outputs == "detectors":
        self._attach_detector_outputs(g, first_port)
    else:
        for v in [*self._detectors, *self.observables]:
            g.remove_vertex(v)
        if outputs == "records":
            self._attach_record_outputs(g, first_port)
    if closed:
        for v in [*self._records, *self._silent_records]:
            g.set_vertex_label(v, None)
    return g

Source code in src/tsim/core/builder.py 
def correlated_error(
    self,
    qubits: list[int],
    types: list[Literal["X", "Y", "Z"]],
    p: float,
) -> None:
    """Add a correlated error term affecting multiple qubits with given Pauli types.

    Its noise spiders get their error bit in ``finalize_correlated_error``,
    which must run before the graph is built. Raises ``ValueError``, and
    changes nothing, if ``qubits`` and ``types`` differ in length.
    """
    targets = list(zip(qubits, types, strict=True))
    term = len(self._correlated_error_probs)
    for qubit, type_ in targets:
        if type_ == "X" or type_ == "Y":
            self._pending_correlated.append(
                (self.spider(qubit, VertexType.X), term)
            )
        if type_ == "Z" or type_ == "Y":
            self._pending_correlated.append(
                (self.spider(qubit, VertexType.Z), term)
            )
    self._correlated_error_probs.append(p)

def cz(
    self,
    control: int,
    target: int,
    classically_controlled: list[bool] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Apply CZ; ``classically_controlled`` marks record targets (``rec[-k]``)."""
    if classically_controlled and classically_controlled[1]:
        if classically_controlled[0]:
            # NOTE: a CZ between two measurement records only phases classical
            # bits, so it does nothing (as in Stim).
            return
        # NOTE: CZ is symmetric, so the record becomes the control.
        classically_controlled = classically_controlled[::-1]
        control, target = target, control
    self._controlled(
        VertexType.Z, EdgeType.HADAMARD, control, target, classically_controlled
    )

finalize_correlated_error() -> None

Finalize the current correlated error channel.

Adds the channel (2^k outcomes for its k terms), gives each pending noise spider its term's error bit, and clears the pending state.

Source code in src/tsim/core/builder.py 
def finalize_correlated_error(self) -> None:
    """Finalize the current correlated error channel.

    Adds the channel (``2^k`` outcomes for its ``k`` terms), gives each
    pending noise spider its term's error bit, and clears the pending state.
    """
    if not self._correlated_error_probs:
        return
    first = self.add_channel(correlated_error_probs(self._correlated_error_probs))
    for v, term in self._pending_correlated:
        self._graph.set_phase(v, error_phase(first + term))
    self._pending_correlated = []
    self._correlated_error_probs = []

def include_observable(self, record_indices: list[int], index: int) -> None:
    """XOR the given measurement records into observable ``index``.

    The observable is created on first use, as in Stim's
    ``OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE``; with no records, that is all this does.
    """
    index = int(index)

    if index not in self._observables:
        v0 = self._graph.add_vertex(
            VertexType.X,
            col=self._annotation_col(record_indices),
            row=ANNOTATION_ROW,
            domain=Domain.CLASSICAL,
            label=f"obs[{index}]",
        )
        self._observables[index] = v0

    v0 = self._observables[index]
    for record_index in record_indices:
        self._xor_record(v0, record_index)

A silent measurement is not recorded; it is labelled m[i]. Returns the measurement's classical spider.

Source code in src/tsim/core/builder.py 
def measure(self, qubit: int, *, silent: bool = False) -> Vertex:
    """Measure a qubit in the Z basis and record it as ``rec[i]``.

    A silent measurement is not recorded; it is labelled ``m[i]``. Returns
    the measurement's classical spider.
    """
    self._ensure_lane(qubit)
    v1 = self._last_vertex[qubit]
    self._graph.set_vertex_type(v1, VertexType.Z)
    self._graph.merge_mirror_copies(v1)
    if not silent:
        self._graph.set_vertex_label(v1, f"rec[{len(self._records)}]")
        self._records.append(v1)
    else:
        self._graph.set_vertex_label(v1, f"m[{len(self._silent_records)}]")
        self._silent_records.append(v1)
    v2 = self._add_quantum_boundary(qubit)
    self._graph.add_edge(v1, v2)
    return v1

def reset(self, qubit: int) -> None:
    """Reset a qubit to ``|0⟩``.

    If the qubit does not yet have a lane, create one in the reset state.
    Otherwise, silently measure the existing lane to trace out the previous
    state before reconnecting the qubit in the reset state.
    """
    if qubit not in self._last_vertex:
        self._graph.plug_basis(self._add_lane(qubit))
        return
    self.measure(qubit, silent=True)
    col = self._last_col(qubit)
    v1 = self._last_vertex[qubit]
    (v2,) = self._graph.neighbors(v1)
    self._graph.remove_edge(v1, v2)
    self._graph.plug_basis(v1)
    v3 = self._add_quantum_boundary(qubit, col + 1)
    self._graph.add_edge(v1, v3)

spider(

    vertex_type: VertexType,
    phase: Phase | Fraction | None = None,
    *,
    col: float | None = None

Turn the trailing boundary of a qubit's wire into a quantum spider.

The spider keeps the boundary's quantum domain, moves to column col if given, and a new quantum boundary is appended after it. Returns the spider.

Source code in src/tsim/core/builder.py 
def spider(
    self,
    qubit: int,
    vertex_type: VertexType,
    phase: Phase | Fraction | None = None,
    *,
    col: float | None = None,
) -> Vertex:
    """Turn the trailing boundary of a qubit's wire into a quantum spider.

    The spider keeps the boundary's quantum domain, moves to column ``col``
    if given, and a new quantum boundary is appended after it. Returns the
    spider.
    """
    self._ensure_lane(qubit)
    v1 = self._last_vertex[qubit]
    self._graph.set_vertex_type(v1, vertex_type)
    if col is not None:
        self._graph.set_col(v1, col)
    if phase is not None:
        self._graph.set_phase(v1, phase)
    v2 = self._add_quantum_boundary(qubit)
    self._graph.add_edge(v1, v2)
    return v1

def swap(self, qubit1: int, qubit2: int) -> None:
    """Swap two wires by exchanging their ends (and rows)."""
    self._ensure_lane(qubit1)
    self._ensure_lane(qubit2)

    v1 = self._last_vertex[qubit1]
    v2 = self._last_vertex[qubit2]
    self._last_vertex[qubit1] = v2
    self._last_vertex[qubit2] = v1

    # NOTE: both wire ends move to the later column first, so neither lands on
    # a position the other lane already uses.
    col = max(self._graph.col(v1), self._graph.col(v2))
    self._graph.set_col(v1, col)
    self._graph.set_col(v2, col)
    self._graph.set_row(v1, qubit2)
    self._graph.set_row(v2, qubit1)

def tick(self) -> None:
    """Align all wire ends to the same column."""

    """Initialize from coefficients and optional power.

    The value represented is (c_0 + c_1*omega + c_2*omega^2 + c_3*omega^3) * 2^power
    where omega = e^{i*pi/4}.

Compute product along the specified axis using associative scan.

Returns identity (1+0i with power 0) for empty reductions.

def prod(self, axis: int = -1) -> "ExactScalarArray":
    """Compute product along the specified axis using associative scan.

    Returns identity (1+0i with power 0) for empty reductions.

    Args:
        axis: The axis along which to compute the product.

    Returns:
        ExactScalarArray with the product computed along the axis.

    """
    if axis < 0:
        axis += self.power.ndim

    if self.coeffs.shape[axis] == 0:
        # Product of empty sequence is identity: [1, 0, 0, 0] * 2^0
        coeffs_shape = self.coeffs.shape[:axis] + self.coeffs.shape[axis + 1 :]
        result_coeffs = jnp.zeros(coeffs_shape, dtype=self.coeffs.dtype)
        result_coeffs = result_coeffs.at[..., 0].set(1)
        return ExactScalarArray(result_coeffs)

    result_power, result_coeffs = _reduce_along_scan(
        self.power,
        self.coeffs,
        _scalar_mul_with_power,
        axis,
    )
    return ExactScalarArray(result_coeffs, result_power)

    circuit: Circuit, *, sample_detectors: bool

Prepare a circuit for compilation.

  1. Parse the stim circuit into a quantum/classical ZX graph.
  2. Close it into a sampling graph with classical outputs.
  3. Reduce it with zxparam's full_reduce.
  4. Rewrite error bits as error-basis bits (Gaussian elimination).
  5. Reset the scalar (normalization is computed separately).
Source code in src/tsim/core/graph.py 
def prepare_graph(circuit: Circuit, *, sample_detectors: bool) -> SamplingGraph:
    """Prepare a circuit for compilation.

    1. Parse the stim circuit into a quantum/classical ZX graph.
    2. Close it into a sampling graph with classical outputs.
    3. Reduce it with zxparam's ``full_reduce``.
    4. Rewrite error bits as error-basis bits (Gaussian elimination).
    5. Reset the scalar (normalization is computed separately).
    """
    builder = parse_stim_circuit(circuit._stim_circ)
    graph = builder.build(
        closed=True, outputs="detectors" if sample_detectors else "records"
    )
    zxparam.full_reduce(graph)
    graph, error_transform = transform_error_basis(graph, builder.num_error_bits)
    graph.scalar = Scalar.one()
    return SamplingGraph(
        graph=graph,
        error_transform=error_transform,
        channel_probs=builder.channel_probs,
        num_outputs=len(graph.outputs()),
        num_detectors=len(builder.detectors),
        layout=ParamLayout(builder.num_error_bits),
    )

Finds a linearly independent basis over GF(2) for the parity sets on the graph's vertices and rewrites each vertex's error IDs as basis IDs (ParamLayout(num_errors).basis(j)). Output-connected spiders come first, so basis bits are numbered in output order where possible, which helps the direct path avoid a reindex.

def transform_error_basis(g: Graph, num_errors: int) -> tuple[Graph, np.ndarray]:
    """Rewrite error parameters in a smaller basis of error-basis bits.

    Finds a linearly independent basis over GF(2) for the parity sets on the
    graph's vertices and rewrites each vertex's error IDs as basis IDs
    (``ParamLayout(num_errors).basis(j)``). Output-connected spiders come first,
    so basis bits are numbered in output order where possible, which helps the
    direct path avoid a reindex.

    Args:
        g: A graph whose vertex parameters are error IDs ``0 … num_errors − 1``.
        num_errors: The number of error bits.

    Returns:
        The graph (mutated in place) and a binary matrix of shape
        ``(num_basis, num_errors)`` whose row ``j`` lists the errors whose XOR is
        basis bit ``j``.

    """
    layout = ParamLayout(num_errors)
    near_outputs = [n for b in g.outputs() for n in g.neighbors(b)]
    parametrized = list(
        dict.fromkeys(
            v for v in [*near_outputs, *g.vertices()] if g.phase(v).parameters
        )
    )
    error_matrix = np.zeros((len(parametrized), num_errors), dtype=np.uint8)
    for row, v in enumerate(parametrized):
        params = sorted(g.phase(v).parameters)
        if params[-1] >= num_errors:
            raise ValueError(f"vertex {v} carries a parameter that is not an error bit")
        error_matrix[row, params] = 1

    basis, transform = find_basis(error_matrix)
    for v, transform_row in zip(parametrized, transform, strict=True):
        ids = frozenset(layout.basis(int(j)) for j in np.nonzero(transform_row)[0])
        g.set_phase(v, Phase(g.phase(v).value, ids))
    return g, basis

Apply heralded single-qubit Pauli channel.

Records a herald bit into the measurement record. When the channel fires (with total probability pi+px+py+pz), the herald is 1 and one of I/X/Y/Z is applied. When it doesn't fire, the herald is 0 and nothing happens.

Source code in src/tsim/core/instructions.py 
def heralded_pauli_channel_1(
    builder: GraphBuilder,
    qubit: int,
    pi: float,
    px: float,
    py: float,
    pz: float,
) -> None:
    """Apply heralded single-qubit Pauli channel.

    Records a herald bit into the measurement record. When the channel fires
    (with total probability pi+px+py+pz), the herald is 1 and one of I/X/Y/Z
    is applied. When it doesn't fire, the herald is 0 and nothing happens.
    """
    bit = builder.add_channel(heralded_pauli_channel_1_probs(pi, px, py, pz))
    aux = HELPER_LANE
    r(builder, aux)
    builder.spider(aux, VertexType.X, error_phase(bit))  # herald bit flip
    m(builder, aux)
    builder.spider(qubit, VertexType.Z, error_phase(bit + 1))  # Z error bit
    builder.spider(qubit, VertexType.X, error_phase(bit + 2))  # X error bit

def m(builder: GraphBuilder, qubit: int, p: float = 0, invert: bool = False) -> None:
    """Measure qubit in Z basis with optional bit-flip error probability p."""
    if invert:
        x(builder, qubit)
    if p > 0:
        # NOTE: the same X error before and after the measurement flips the
        # record but not the state.
        flip = error_phase(builder.add_channel(error_probs(p)))
        builder.spider(qubit, VertexType.X, flip)
        builder.measure(qubit)
        builder.spider(qubit, VertexType.X, flip)
    else:
        builder.measure(qubit)
    if invert:
        x(builder, qubit)

def r_pauli(
    builder: GraphBuilder,
    paulis: list[tuple[Literal["X", "Y", "Z"], int]],
    theta: Fraction,
    dagger: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Apply exp(-i theta pi/2 P) for a Pauli product P, with theta in half-turns.

    Generalizes ``SPP`` (theta=1/2) and ``TPP`` (theta=1/4) to an arbitrary angle.
    For a single qubit, ``r_pauli`` reduces to the named single-qubit rotation in
    that Pauli's basis (e.g. ``R_PAULI Z0`` is ``R_Z``). If `dagger` is True, apply
    exp(+i theta pi/2 P) instead.

    Args:
        builder: The graph builder to modify.
        paulis: List of (pauli_type, qubit) pairs defining the Pauli product P.
        theta: Rotation angle in half-turns (units of pi).
        dagger: If True, negate the rotation angle.

    """
    _pauli_product_phase(
        builder,
        paulis,
        lambda builder, qubit: r_z(builder, qubit, theta),
        lambda builder, qubit: r_z(builder, qubit, -theta),
        dagger,
    )

def tpp(
    builder: GraphBuilder,
    paulis: list[tuple[Literal["X", "Y", "Z"], int]],
    dagger: bool = False,
) -> None:
    """Apply exp(-i pi/8 P) (up to global phase) for a Pauli product P.

    Phases the -1 eigenspace of P by exp(i pi/4) (or exp(-i pi/4) if dagger).
    For a single qubit, ``TPP Z0`` is the T gate and ``TPP_DAG Z0`` is T_DAG.

    Args:
        builder: The graph builder to modify.
        paulis: List of (pauli_type, qubit) pairs defining the Pauli product P.
        dagger: If True, apply exp(+i pi/8 P) (phase by exp(-i pi/4)) instead.

    """
    _pauli_product_phase(builder, paulis, t, t_dag, dagger)

Supports gates: R_Z, R_X, R_Y, U3.

Parameters:

The stim instruction whose tag will be parsed.

Source code in src/tsim/core/parse.py 
def parse_parametric_tag(
    instruction: stim.CircuitInstruction,
) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Fraction]] | None:
    """Parse the parametric tag on an instruction (e.g. ``I[R_Z(theta=0.3*pi)]``).

    Supports gates: R_Z, R_X, R_Y, U3.

    Args:
        instruction: The stim instruction whose tag will be parsed.

    Returns:
        Tuple of (gate_name, params_dict) when the instruction's tag is a
        well-formed parametric tag, or ``None`` when the tag is not
        parametric-looking (no ``name(...)`` shape, or empty).

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the tag looks parametric (matches ``name(...)``) but is
            malformed: a parameter value does not parse, the gate name is unknown,
            or the parameter keys do not match the expected set for the gate.

    """
    tag = instruction.tag
    err_prefix = f"Could not parse instruction {str(instruction)!r}"

    match = re.match(r"^(\w+)\((.*)\)$", tag)
    if not match:
        return None

    gate_name = match.group(1)
    params_str = match.group(2)

    params = {}
    for param in params_str.split(","):
        param = param.strip()
        if not param:
            continue
        # Match param=value*pi (value can be negative/decimal/scientific)
        param_match = re.match(
            r"^(\w+)=([-+]?(?:\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)(?:[eE][-+]?\d+)?)\*pi$", param
        )
        if not param_match:
            raise ValueError(f"{err_prefix}. Malformed parametric tag {tag!r}")
        param_name = param_match.group(1)
        value = Fraction(param_match.group(2))
        params[param_name] = value

    expected = _PARAMETRIC_GATE_PARAMS.get(gate_name)
    if expected is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{err_prefix}. Unknown parametric gate {gate_name!r}")
    if params.keys() != expected:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{err_prefix}. Parametric tag {tag!r} has parameters "
            f"{sorted(params)}, expected {sorted(expected)}"
        )

    return gate_name, params

Parameters:

Returns:

Source code in src/tsim/core/parse.py 
def parse_stim_circuit(stim_circuit: stim.Circuit) -> GraphBuilder:
    """Parse a stim circuit into a GraphBuilder.

    Args:
        stim_circuit: The stim circuit to convert.

    Returns:
        A GraphBuilder containing the ZX graph and all auxiliary data.

    """
    builder = GraphBuilder()

    for instruction in stim_circuit.flattened():
        assert not isinstance(instruction, stim.CircuitRepeatBlock)

        name = instruction.name
        if name == "SHIFT_COORDS":

            # TODO: handle visualization annotations in ZX diagrams
            continue

        if any(t.is_sweep_bit_target for t in instruction.targets_copy()):
            raise NotImplementedError(
                f"Sweep bit targets (e.g. sweep[N]) are not supported "
                f"in instruction {str(instruction)!r}"
            )

        if name == "S" and is_t_tag(instruction.tag):
            name = "T"
        elif name == "S_DAG" and is_t_tag(instruction.tag):
            name = "T_DAG"

        # Handle parametric gates via tags (e.g., I with tag "R_Z(theta=0.3*pi)")
        if name == "I" and instruction.tag:
            result = parse_parametric_tag(instruction)
            if result is not None:
                gate_name, params = result
                targets = [t.value for t in instruction.targets_copy()]
                for qubit in targets:
                    if gate_name == "R_Z":
                        r_z(builder, qubit, params["theta"])
                    elif gate_name == "R_X":
                        r_x(builder, qubit, params["theta"])
                    elif gate_name == "R_Y":
                        r_y(builder, qubit, params["theta"])
                    elif gate_name == "U3":
                        u3(
                            builder,
                            qubit,
                            params["theta"],
                            params["phi"],
                            params["lambda"],
                        )
                    else:
                        raise ValueError(f"Unknown parametric gate: {gate_name}")
                continue

        if name == "TICK":
            builder.tick()
            continue
        if name == "MPP":
            args = instruction.gate_args_copy()
            p = args[0] if args else 0
            for paulis, invert in _iter_pauli_products(instruction):
                mpp(builder, paulis, invert, p=p)
            continue
        if name in ("SPP", "SPP_DAG") and is_t_tag(instruction.tag):
            is_dag = name == "SPP_DAG"
            for paulis, invert in _iter_pauli_products(instruction):
                tpp(builder, paulis, dagger=is_dag ^ invert)
            continue
        if name in ("SPP", "SPP_DAG") and instruction.tag:
            parsed = parse_parametric_tag(instruction)
            if parsed is not None and parsed[0] == "R_PAULI":
                params = parsed[1]
                _validate_r_pauli_targets(instruction)
                is_dag = name == "SPP_DAG"
                for paulis, invert in _iter_pauli_products(instruction):
                    r_pauli(builder, paulis, params["theta"], dagger=is_dag ^ invert)
                continue
        if name in ("SPP", "SPP_DAG"):
            is_dag = name == "SPP_DAG"
            for paulis, invert in _iter_pauli_products(instruction):
                spp(builder, paulis, dagger=is_dag ^ invert)
            continue
        if name == "MPAD":
            args = instruction.gate_args_copy()
            p = args[0] if args else 0
            for target in instruction.targets_copy():
                mpad(builder, target.value, p=p)
            continue
        if name == "E" or name == "ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR":
            if name == "E":
                builder.finalize_correlated_error()
            targets = [t.value for t in instruction.targets_copy()]
            types: list[Literal["X", "Y", "Z"]] = []
            for t in instruction.targets_copy():
                if t.is_x_target:
                    types.append("X")
                elif t.is_y_target:
                    types.append("Y")
                elif t.is_z_target:
                    types.append("Z")
                else:
                    raise ValueError(f"Invalid target: {t}")
            builder.correlated_error(targets, types, instruction.gate_args_copy()[0])
            continue
        if name == "DETECTOR":
            targets = [t.value for t in instruction.targets_copy()]
            builder.add_detector(targets)
            continue
        if name == "OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE":
            targets_copy = instruction.targets_copy()
            for t in targets_copy:
                if not t.is_measurement_record_target:
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE with Pauli targets is not "
                        f"supported in Tsim (only measurement record targets "
                        f"like rec[-1] are supported). Got instruction "
                        f"{str(instruction)!r}"
                    )
            targets = [t.value for t in targets_copy]
            args = instruction.gate_args_copy()
            builder.include_observable(targets, int(args[0]))
            continue

        # instruction dispatch
        if name not in GATE_TABLE:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown gate: {name}")

        gate_func, num_qubits = GATE_TABLE[name]
        targets = [t.value for t in instruction.targets_copy()]
        invert = [t.is_inverted_result_target for t in instruction.targets_copy()]
        is_classically_controlled = [
            t.is_measurement_record_target for t in instruction.targets_copy()
        ]
        args = instruction.gate_args_copy()

        for i_target in range(0, len(targets), num_qubits):
            chunk = targets[i_target : i_target + num_qubits]
            cc_chunk = is_classically_controlled[i_target : i_target + num_qubits]
            chunk_inverted = False
            for j in range(num_qubits):
                chunk_inverted ^= invert[i_target + j]
            assert not (invert[i_target] and is_classically_controlled[i_target])
            if chunk_inverted:
                gate_func(builder, *chunk, *args, invert=True)
            elif any(cc_chunk):
                gate_func(builder, *chunk, *args, classically_controlled=cc_chunk)
            else:
                gate_func(builder, *chunk, *args)

    builder.finalize_correlated_error()

    # NOTE: materialize every observable id from 0..num_observables-1 so missing
    # indices appear as deterministic-zero outputs, matching Stim semantics.
    # Including no records into an existing observable does nothing.
    for i in range(stim_circuit.num_observables):
        builder.include_observable([], i)

    return builder

def __post_init__(self) -> None:
    """Validate channel probabilities."""
    # NOTE: NumPy's overhead dominates for a channel's few outcomes, and
    # simplification makes many channels, so the range is checked in plain
    # Python and the sum without np.isclose, with its tolerance.
    tol = 1e-6
    values = self.probs.tolist()
    if min(values, default=0.0) < -tol or max(values, default=0.0) > 1.0 + tol:
        raise ValueError(f"Probabilities must lie in [0, 1], but got: {self.probs}")
    if not abs(float(self.probs.sum()) - 1.0) <= 1e-8 + 1e-5:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Probabilities must sum to 1, but got: {self.probs} "
            f"(sum {np.sum(self.probs)})"
        )

ChannelSampler(
    channel_probs: list[ndarray],
    error_transform: ndarray,
    seed: int | None = None,

Samples from multiple error channels and transforms to a reduced basis.

This class combines multiple error channels (each producing error bits e0, e1, ...) and applies a linear transformation over GF(2) to convert samples from the original "e" basis to a reduced "f" basis using geometric-skip sampling optimized for low-noise regimes.

f_i = error_transform_ij * e_j mod 2. Within each channel, probability-array bit 0 corresponds to the first produced error bit, bit 1 to the second, and so on.

Channels are automatically simplified by: 1. Removing bits e_i that do not affect any f-variable (i.e. all-zero columns in error_transform) 2. Folding duplicate column IDs, i.e. channels whose column signatures contain duplicate IDs. 3. Merging channels with identical column signatures, i.e. channels whose corresponding columns in error_transform are identical. 4. Absorbing channels whose signatures are subsets of others, i.e. channels whose corresponding columns in error_transform are a strict subset of another channel's columns.

Example

probs = [error_probs(0.1), error_probs(0.2)] # two 1-bit channels transform = np.array([[1, 1]]) # f0 = e0 XOR e1 sampler = ChannelSampler(probs, transform) samples = sampler.sample(1000) # shape (1000, 1)

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default channel_probs list[ndarray]

List of probability arrays. Channel i has shape (2^k_i,) and produces k_i error bits starting at index sum(k_0:k_{i-1}). For example, if channels have shapes [(4,), (2,), (4,)], they produce variables [e0,e1], [e2], [e3,e4].

required error_transform ndarray

Binary matrix of shape (num_f, num_e) where entry [i, j] = 1 means f_i depends on e_j. For example, if row 0 is [0, 1, 0, 1], then f0 = e1 XOR e3.

required seed int | None

Random seed for sampling. If None, a random seed is generated.

def __init__(
    self,
    channel_probs: list[np.ndarray],
    error_transform: np.ndarray,
    seed: int | None = None,
):
    """Initialize the sampler with channel probabilities and a basis transformation.

    Args:
        channel_probs: List of probability arrays. Channel i has shape (2^k_i,)
            and produces k_i error bits starting at index sum(k_0:k_{i-1}).
            For example, if channels have shapes [(4,), (2,), (4,)], they
            produce variables [e0,e1], [e2], [e3,e4].
        error_transform: Binary matrix of shape (num_f, num_e) where entry [i, j] = 1
            means f_i depends on e_j. For example, if row 0 is [0, 1, 0, 1],
            then f0 = e1 XOR e3.
        seed: Random seed for sampling. If None, a random seed is generated.

    """
    unique_cols, inverse = unique_columns(error_transform)

    # Signature matrix: each row is a unique column signature
    signature_matrix = unique_cols.T  # shape (num_signatures, num_f)

    # Find null_col_id: the index of the all-zero column (or None)
    zero_col_indices = np.flatnonzero(np.all(unique_cols == 0, axis=0))
    null_col_id = int(zero_col_indices[0]) if len(zero_col_indices) else None

    # Create Channel objects with unique_col_ids from inverse mapping
    channels: list[Channel] = []
    e_offset = 0
    for probs in channel_probs:
        num_bits = channel_num_bits(probs)
        col_ids = tuple(int(inverse[e_offset + i]) for i in range(num_bits))
        channels.append(Channel(probs=probs, unique_col_ids=col_ids))
        e_offset += num_bits

    self.channels = simplify_channels(channels, null_col_id=null_col_id)
    self.signature_matrix = signature_matrix.astype(np.uint8)

    self._rng = np.random.default_rng(
        seed if seed is not None else np.random.default_rng().integers(0, 2**30)
    )
    self._tables = _fire_tables(self.channels, self.signature_matrix)

def block_seeds(self, num_samples: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """Draw the seeds of the blocks of the next ``num_samples`` samples."""

def sample(
    self, num_samples: int = 1, seeds: np.ndarray | None = None
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Sample from all error channels and transform to new error basis.

    Uses geometric-skip sampling, optimized for low-noise regimes where
    P(non-identity) << 1 per channel. Blocks of shots are sampled in
    parallel, each from its own random stream, so the samples depend on the
    seed and ``num_samples`` but not on the number of threads.

    Args:
        num_samples: Number of samples to draw.
        seeds: The blocks' seeds from ``block_seeds(num_samples)``; drawn
            here if ``None``.

    Returns:
        NumPy array of shape (num_samples, num_f) with uint8 values indicating
        which f-variables are set for each sample.

    """
    num_f = self.signature_matrix.shape[1]
    result = np.empty((num_samples, num_f), dtype=np.uint8)
    self._sample_into(result, seeds, self._flip_tables(packed=False))
    return result

def sample_packed(
    self, num_samples: int = 1, seeds: np.ndarray | None = None
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Return ``sample``'s rows bit-packed, as ``sample`` draws them from ``seeds``.

    f-variable ``i`` is bit ``i % 64`` of word ``i // 64``; the bits past
    ``num_f`` are zero.

    Returns:
        NumPy array of shape (num_samples, ceil(num_f / 64)) of uint64.

    """
    num_f = self.signature_matrix.shape[1]
    result = np.empty((num_samples, -(-num_f // 64)), dtype=np.uint64)
    self._sample_into(result, seeds, self._flip_tables(packed=True))
    return result

def absorb_subset_channels(channels: list[Channel], max_bits: int = 4) -> list[Channel]:
    """Absorb channels whose signatures are subsets of others.

    If channel A's signatures are a strict subset of channel B's signatures,
    and |B| <= max_bits, then A is absorbed into B.

    Args:
        channels: List of channels
        max_bits: Maximum number of bits allowed per channel

    Returns:
        List in which no channel is a strict subset of another of at most
        ``max_bits`` signatures

    """
    # NOTE: largest first, so that every channel is absorbed into the first
    # channel that contains it.
    channels = sorted(channels, key=lambda c: -len(c.unique_col_ids))

    # NOTE: a channel of at most max_bits signatures has few strict subsets, so
    # they are looked up instead of compared with every other channel.
    by_signatures: dict[frozenset[int], list[int]] = defaultdict(list)
    for j, channel in enumerate(channels):
        by_signatures[frozenset(channel.unique_col_ids)].append(j)

    result: list[Channel] = []
    absorbed: set[int] = set()

    for i, channel_i in enumerate(channels):
        if i in absorbed:
            continue

        signatures = sorted(set(channel_i.unique_col_ids))
        current_probs = channel_i.probs.copy()
        current_col_ids = channel_i.unique_col_ids

        if len(signatures) <= max_bits:
            subsets = (
                frozenset(subset)
                for size in range(len(signatures))
                for subset in combinations(signatures, size)
            )
            subset_channels = sorted(
                j
                for subset in subsets
                for j in by_signatures.get(subset, ())
                if j > i and j not in absorbed
            )
            for j in subset_channels:
                # Expand channel_j to match channel_i's signatures and convolve
                expanded_j = expand_channel(channels[j], current_col_ids)
                current_probs = xor_convolve(current_probs, expanded_j.probs)
                absorbed.add(j)

        result.append(Channel(probs=current_probs, unique_col_ids=current_col_ids))

    return result

def channel_num_bits(probs: np.ndarray) -> int:
    """Return the number of bits ``k`` of a channel with ``2^k`` outcomes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the number of outcomes is not a power of two.

    """
    num_bits = len(probs).bit_length() - 1
    if num_bits < 0 or len(probs) != 1 << num_bits:
        raise ValueError(f"a channel has 2^k outcomes, but got {len(probs)}")
    return num_bits

Build probability distribution for correlated error chain.

Given conditional probabilities [p1, p2, ..., pk] from a chain of CORRELATED_ERROR(p1) ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR(p2) ... ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR(pk), computes the joint probability distribution over 2^k outcomes.

Since errors are mutually exclusive, only outcomes with at most one bit set have non-zero probability. - probs[0] is the probability that no branch fires. - probs[1 << i] is the probability that branch i fires after all previous branches did not fire.

def correlated_error_probs(probabilities: list[float]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Build probability distribution for correlated error chain.

    Given conditional probabilities [p1, p2, ..., pk] from a chain of
    CORRELATED_ERROR(p1) ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR(p2) ... ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR(pk),
    computes the joint probability distribution over 2^k outcomes.

    Since errors are mutually exclusive, only outcomes with at most one bit set
    have non-zero probability.
    - ``probs[0]`` is the probability that no branch fires.
    - ``probs[1 << i]`` is the probability that branch ``i`` fires after all
      previous branches did not fire.

    Args:
        probabilities: List of conditional probabilities [p1, p2, ..., pk]

    Returns:
        Array of shape (2^k,) with probabilities for each outcome.

    """
    k = len(probabilities)
    probs = np.zeros(2**k, dtype=np.float64)

    no_error_so_far = 1.0
    for i, p in enumerate(probabilities):
        probs[1 << i] = no_error_so_far * p
        no_error_so_far *= 1 - p

    probs[0] = no_error_so_far
    return probs

def expand_channel(channel: Channel, target_col_ids: tuple[int, ...]) -> Channel:
    """Expand a channel's distribution to a larger signature set.

    The channel's existing column IDs must be a strict subset of
    ``target_col_ids`` when considered as sets, and both tuples must be sorted.
    New target bit positions are treated as always zero.

    Duplicate source column IDs are allowed. When multiple source bits map to
    the same target bit, their contribution is XORed, matching GF(2)
    composition. Duplicate target column IDs are not allowed; channels with
    duplicate IDs should be canonicalized before subset absorption.

    Args:
        channel: Channel to expand (must have sorted unique_col_ids)
        target_col_ids: Target signature set (must be sorted superset)

    Returns:
        New channel with expanded distribution

    """
    source_col_ids = channel.unique_col_ids
    if source_col_ids != tuple(sorted(source_col_ids)):
        raise ValueError("Source must be sorted")
    if target_col_ids != tuple(sorted(target_col_ids)):
        raise ValueError("Target must be sorted")
    if len(set(target_col_ids)) != len(target_col_ids):
        raise ValueError("Target must not contain duplicates")
    if not set(source_col_ids) < set(target_col_ids):
        raise ValueError("Source must be strict subset")

    # Map source columns to their positions in target
    source_to_target = {s: target_col_ids.index(s) for s in source_col_ids}
    n_target = len(target_col_ids)
    new_probs = np.zeros(2**n_target, dtype=np.float64)

    for old_idx in range(len(channel.probs)):
        # Map old bit pattern to the expanded pattern.
        # Use XOR so duplicate source columns cancel mod 2.
        new_idx = 0
        for src_pos, src_col in enumerate(source_col_ids):
            if (old_idx >> src_pos) & 1:
                new_idx ^= 1 << source_to_target[src_col]
        new_probs[new_idx] += channel.probs[old_idx]

    return Channel(probs=new_probs, unique_col_ids=target_col_ids)

def fold_duplicate_channel_bits(channels: list[Channel]) -> list[Channel]:
    """Canonicalize channels by XOR-folding duplicate column IDs.

    If two bits in the same channel have identical column signatures, sampling
    both bits only affects the reduced error basis through their parity. This
    replaces those duplicate bits with one bit whose probability is the sum of
    all old outcomes with the same XOR-folded value.

    Args:
        channels: List of channels with sorted unique_col_ids

    Returns:
        List of channels whose unique_col_ids contain no duplicates

    """
    result: list[Channel] = []

    for channel in channels:
        old_col_ids = channel.unique_col_ids
        new_col_ids = tuple(dict.fromkeys(old_col_ids))

        if len(new_col_ids) == len(old_col_ids):
            result.append(channel)
            continue

        col_to_new_pos = {col: pos for pos, col in enumerate(new_col_ids)}
        new_probs = np.zeros(2 ** len(new_col_ids), dtype=np.float64)

        for old_idx in range(len(channel.probs)):
            new_idx = 0
            for old_pos, col in enumerate(old_col_ids):
                if (old_idx >> old_pos) & 1:
                    new_idx ^= 1 << col_to_new_pos[col]
            new_probs[new_idx] += channel.probs[old_idx]

        result.append(Channel(probs=new_probs, unique_col_ids=new_col_ids))

    return result

def heralded_pauli_channel_1_probs(
    pi: float, px: float, py: float, pz: float
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Heralded single-qubit Pauli channel. Returns shape (8,).

    Bit layout:
    - bit 0: herald bit, written to the measurement record
    - bit 1: Z error component
    - bit 2: X error component

    The non-zero outcomes are:
    - index 0 (0b000): no herald, no Pauli error
    - index 1 (0b001): herald + I
    - index 3 (0b011): herald + Z
    - index 5 (0b101): herald + X
    - index 7 (0b111): herald + Y, represented as X+Z
    """
    probs = np.zeros(8, dtype=np.float64)
    probs[0] = 1 - pi - px - py - pz
    probs[1] = pi
    probs[3] = pz
    probs[5] = px
    probs[7] = py
    return probs

def merge_identical_channels(channels: list[Channel]) -> list[Channel]:
    """Merge all channels with identical signature sets.

    Groups channels by their unique_col_ids and convolves all channels
    in each group into a single channel.

    Args:
        channels: List of channels

    Returns:
        List with at most one channel per unique signature set

    """
    groups: dict[tuple[int, ...], list[Channel]] = defaultdict(list)

    for channel in channels:
        key = channel.unique_col_ids
        groups[key].append(channel)

    result: list[Channel] = []

    for col_ids, group in groups.items():
        if len(group) == 1:
            result.append(group[0])
        else:
            # Convolve all channels in the group
            combined_probs = group[0].probs.copy()
            for channel in group[1:]:
                combined_probs = xor_convolve(combined_probs, channel.probs)
            result.append(Channel(probs=combined_probs, unique_col_ids=col_ids))

    return result

def normalize_channels(channels: list[Channel]) -> list[Channel]:
    """Normalize channels by sorting unique_col_ids, permuting probs accordingly.

    This ensures channels affecting the same set of columns have identical
    ``unique_col_ids`` tuples, enabling ``merge_identical_channels`` to group
    them. The probability tensor is transposed using the same axis permutation
    so little-endian outcome bits continue to refer to the matching column IDs.

    Args:
        channels: List of channels

    Returns:
        List of channels with sorted unique_col_ids

    """
    result: list[Channel] = []

    for channel in channels:
        n = channel.num_bits
        source_col_ids = np.array(channel.unique_col_ids)
        axis_perm = np.argsort(source_col_ids, stable=True)
        probs_tensor = channel.probs.reshape((2,) * n, order="F")
        new_probs = probs_tensor.transpose(axis_perm).reshape(2**n, order="F")

        result.append(
            Channel(probs=new_probs, unique_col_ids=tuple(source_col_ids[axis_perm]))
        )

    return result

    pxy: float,
    pxz: float,
    pyi: float,
    pyx: float,
    pyy: float,
    pyz: float,
    pzi: float,
    pzx: float,
    pzy: float,
    pzz: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Two-qubit Pauli channel. Returns shape (16,).

    Bit layout:
    - bit 0: Z error component on ``qubit_i``
    - bit 1: X error component on ``qubit_i``
    - bit 2: Z error component on ``qubit_j``
    - bit 3: X error component on ``qubit_j``

    With that layout, index ``z_i + 2*x_i + 4*z_j + 8*x_j`` stores the
    probability for the corresponding two-qubit Pauli outcome. The arguments
    follow Stim's naming convention: ``pix`` is I on ``qubit_i`` and X on
    ``qubit_j``, ``pzi`` is Z on ``qubit_i`` and I on ``qubit_j``, etc.
    """
    remainder = (
        1
        - pix
        - piy
        - piz
        - pxi
        - pxx
        - pxy
        - pxz
        - pyi
        - pyx
        - pyy
        - pyz
        - pzi
        - pzx
        - pzy
        - pzz
    )
    probs = np.array(
        [
            remainder,  # index 0 (0b0000): II
            pzi,  # index 1 (0b0001): ZI
            pxi,  # index 2 (0b0010): XI
            pyi,  # index 3 (0b0011): YI
            piz,  # index 4 (0b0100): IZ
            pzz,  # index 5 (0b0101): ZZ
            pxz,  # index 6 (0b0110): XZ
            pyz,  # index 7 (0b0111): YZ
            pix,  # index 8 (0b1000): IX
            pzx,  # index 9 (0b1001): ZX
            pxx,  # index 10 (0b1010): XX
            pyx,  # index 11 (0b1011): YX
            piy,  # index 12 (0b1100): IY
            pzy,  # index 13 (0b1101): ZY
            pxy,  # index 14 (0b1110): XY
            pyy,  # index 15 (0b1111): YY
        ],
        dtype=np.float64,
    )
    return probs

def reduce_null_bits(
    channels: list[Channel], null_col_id: int | None = None
) -> list[Channel]:
    """Remove bits corresponding to the null column (all-zero column).

    If a channel has bits mapped to null_col_id (representing an all-zero
    column in the transform matrix), those bits don't affect any f-variable
    and can be marginalized out by summing over them.

    Args:
        channels: List of channels
        null_col_id: Column ID representing the all-zero column, or None if
            there is no all-zero column.

    Returns:
        List of channels with null bits marginalized out. Channels with all
        null entries are removed entirely (they have no effect on outputs).

    """
    if null_col_id is None:
        # No null column, nothing to reduce
        return channels

    result: list[Channel] = []

    for channel in channels:
        n = channel.num_bits
        non_null_positions = [
            i
            for i, col_id in enumerate(channel.unique_col_ids)
            if col_id != null_col_id
        ]

        if len(non_null_positions) == 0:
            # All entries are null, channel has no effect - remove it
            continue

        # Marginalize out null bits by summing their tensor axes. The Fortran
        # order reshape makes axis i correspond to little-endian bit i.
        new_col_ids = tuple(channel.unique_col_ids[i] for i in non_null_positions)
        new_num_bits = len(non_null_positions)
        sum_axes = tuple(i for i in range(n) if i not in non_null_positions)
        probs_tensor = channel.probs.reshape((2,) * n, order="F")
        new_probs = probs_tensor.sum(axis=sum_axes).reshape(2**new_num_bits, order="F")

        result.append(Channel(probs=new_probs, unique_col_ids=new_col_ids))

    return result

def simplify_channels(
    channels: list[Channel], max_bits: int = 4, null_col_id: int | None = None
) -> list[Channel]:
    """Simplify channels by removing null columns, folding, merging identical and absorbing subsets.

    Args:
        channels: List of channels to simplify
        max_bits: Maximum number of bits allowed per channel
        null_col_id: Column ID representing the all-zero column, or None if
            there is no all-zero column.

    Returns:
        Simplified list of channels

    """
    channels = reduce_null_bits(channels, null_col_id)
    channels = normalize_channels(channels)
    channels = fold_duplicate_channel_bits(channels)
    channels = merge_identical_channels(channels)
    channels = absorb_subset_channels(channels, max_bits)
    return channels

np.unique sorts every column, comparing whole columns, which is slow for a large sparse matrix. Here a dict over the bit-packed columns finds the distinct ones, and only those are sorted, as bytes. Big-endian packing keeps the lexicographic order of the columns, so the result is the same.
